name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 district with strong Democratic fundamentals
Incumbent George Latimer running for reelection
model.rationale: The baseline's D+23.9 margin rests on a heavily Democratic seat, an incumbent Democrat, and a generic underfunded Republican opponent with no reported fundraising. Prediction markets at 96% Democratic confirm Safe D; no evidence justifies moving off the baseline.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing Latimer underperforming or significant outside spending for the challenger would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-16 is a heavily Democratic Westchester-area district where first-term incumbent George Latimer is seeking reelection after winning the seat in 2024. The district's partisan lean of D+18, combined with a modestly favorable national environment and incumbency advantages, gives Democrats a strong structural edge. Latimer has raised over half a million dollars, while Republican Joseph Cinquemani reports no fundraising figures, suggesting a low-budget challenge.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast relies on fundamentals and prediction markets. Polymarket prices a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent, consistent with the quantitative baseline of a D+23.9 margin. With no evidence pointing to a competitive race, this remains Safe Democratic, though the absence of polling adds some uncertainty.
